dedupe_keys.name: agent based model of building occupant behaviour during load shedding

description: This framework studies what load shedding, cutting a building's power use at grid peaks, does to the people inside. It is based on experience in two office buildings near Philadelphia that differ in how much occupants can control and what adaptive actions they have, and generalises it as what-if scenarios for building managers and tenants. EnergyPlus and NetLogo are coupled so that occupants with different thermal and lighting preferences adjust clothing or use portable fans when central controls do not respond, under a corporate dress code and imperfect communication with building managers. It was published by Handi Chandra Putra on CoMSES in May 2020 with a paper in Building Simulation. Coverage: two US office buildings. Access: free code on CoMSES. Licence: GPL-3.0. Caveats: calibrated to two buildings. Simulation uses are comfort impacts of demand response and grid emergencies, and indoor conditions when building systems are curtailed. Related records: EnergyPlus and the office electricity consumption agent-based model.
